body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Four camp talks about Cordelia's personal story, the Thread of Evolution. The companion is CORDELIA SKEIN (call them Cordelia in NARRATOR rows). The attached note is the voice sheet and the fact sheet; it describes an older plan for the Thread's beats in places, so take people, objects, manner and background from it, but where it disagrees with THE FIXED FACTS in this brief, the fixed facts win.

HOW A CAMP TALK WORKS. After a rest the player can walk up to a companion who has asked for a word at the fire. It is private, short and warm. The companion speaks first (NARRATOR and SAY rows), the player chooses what the party says from three short options (or two where the talk says so), and the companion answers in their own voice (a REPLY). Then the talk ends. Nothing in it is a roll or a failure, and every reply must leave the talk finished and the fire going: a cool reply is still an ending, never a slammed door. Each reply also carries a REASON row: one sentence beginning "You", past tense, under 14 words, saying what the party did or said as the companion would remember it (for example "You heard me out at the fire" or "You waved it off and went to bed"). A REASON is plain notice text and is not spoken.

THE FIXED FACTS (the beats in the game's journal; the talks tell these, in Cordelia's own words, and go no further than they do).
- Cordelia's Thread: Cordelia's Evolution. What Cordelia wants: Finish the change someone else began in her, on her own terms.
- The Connection already happened in Wickermoor, with Thomasin Ardor, the tailor. The journal says: "Thomasin took Cordelia's measure, and neither of them said what the fitting was really for."
- The Discovery, "The Second Monograph", happens in Memory's Rest. The journal's line for it: "In Memory's Rest Cordelia found the rest of the dead scholar's notes, and the stage after the one she is in."
- The Confrontation, "The Final Stage", happens in the Crooked Nightmare. The journal's line for it: "In the Crooked Nightmare Cordelia let the change run, and stayed herself."
Each talk is had at camp AFTER its chapter is over, so Cordelia looks back on what happened. You may name Memory's Rest in the Discovery and the Crooked Nightmare in the Confrontation and no other place. Do not describe fights, bosses or villains; Cordelia speaks of what was found, felt or chosen.

THE INCITEMENT AS IT PLAYED (for the first talk). Cordelia sometimes misses this scene because Cordelia is not with the party when it plays in the Jailbird's car of the Ghostlight Express. Then Cordelia goes back alone, and at camp tells the party what was found. These are the facts of the scene; do not change them, you may add small sensory detail:
[evolution_start]
  NARRATOR: Shroud fog presses flat against the Baggage Car glass while the striped prisoner ghost mumbles in his sleep about steak and eggs that never came. Wedged beneath his iron ball and chain sits a cracked leather medical bag smelling sharply of camphor and dried clove.
  CORDELIA: Wait, do hold still and breathe that in. Camphor and clove over old calfskin is the exact preservative scent of a surgical kit.
  NARRATOR: Cordelia's six eyes dilate with an audible click as her lower hands draw out a water-stained monograph titled "On the Final Stage", signed by Doctor Hespa Marlowe. She traces the diagram of a six-chambered vessel in crimson silk-thread that hangs in the air before dissolving into faint red mist.
  CORDELIA: Fascinating pathology, she mapped all six chambers of the thoracic pump without rupturing the outer wall. Doctor Marlowe was not merely patching flesh, she was charting the synthesis of the Apex Humour.
  the party can say: Read the margins aloud. Let us hear her method.
  the party can say: Check the bag for an address before the fog takes it.
  the party can say: Pack the notes. We need to keep moving.
[evolution_read]
  NARRATOR: Cordelia straightens her shoulders, her four lower hands holding the damp pages open with the care of a fellow surgeon at a lecture table. The ruby vials in her thorax catch the lantern light as she reads the cramped notes.
  CORDELIA: Listen to her ratios on venous distillation, it is exquisite work for a single pair of hands. Whoever remade my blood left the metamorphosis half-finished, and with your company, I intend to complete the textbook.
[evolution_traced]
  NARRATOR: Cordelia's upper fingers probe the cracked leather seams of the medical bag until she hooks a brass apothecary tag stamped with a valley clinic mark. She tests the metal edge against her thumb with brisk satisfaction.
  CORDELIA: A practitioner may lose her luggage in the Shroud, but her supplier always stamps the brass. Once we step off these rails, I will follow this clinic mark straight to Doctor Marlowe's operating table.
[evolution_packed]
  NARRATOR: Cordelia folds the water-stained monograph into oilcloth and slips it smoothly inside her coat, her four extra arms tucking close to her ribs. Her six eyes narrow behind a mask of polite, clinical calm.
  CORDELIA: Quite right, the damp in this car is dreadful for unbound paper anyway. I shall review the doctor's thoracic diagrams in private when our walk is done.

THE TALKS. Write these four talks, in this order, with these keys.

TALK incitement. Cordelia tells the party about the Jailbird's car of the Ghostlight Express as one short story at the fire. Opening: 1 NARRATOR row, then 3 or 4 SAY rows (the story, in their own words, ending on a plain statement of how it left them). TWO options only: OPTION 1 asks to hear more or says something that shares the moment; OPTION 2 is the quiet way on, leaving Cordelia to it. Two replies of 1 NARRATOR row (optional) and 1 or 2 SAY rows. No REASON rows in this talk.

TALK discovery. Cordelia has come back from Memory's Rest with the Discovery, and wants to tell it. Opening: 1 NARRATOR row to open the scene at the fire, then 6 to 8 SAY rows (one more NARRATOR row is allowed in the middle) that tell what the journal line says in Cordelia's own words and end on the turn: how it sits with them, with one thing left unsaid (never the dark secret: no names, deeds or places from the note's dark-secret section). Three options: OPTION 1 asks Cordelia to say more; OPTION 2 is the answer most like what Cordelia would want to hear, meeting Cordelia on Cordelia's own terms; OPTION 3 is the quiet way on, civil but brisk, brushing it past. Three replies of 1 to 3 rows each, each ending the talk, each with a REASON row. The cool reply (3) must still leave the Discovery told.

TALK confrontation_wait. Cordelia is at their lowest regard for the party (Strained), and has the Confrontation to tell about the Crooked Nightmare but is holding it back until things are mended. This talk is short. Opening: 1 NARRATOR row and 3 or 4 SAY rows: Cordelia says there is something to say about it and it will keep, and says, in Cordelia's own voice, what matters to Cordelia and that the party's way has drifted from it (do not claim any specific deed the party did). Three options: OPTION 1 listens and owns it (the way to mend); OPTION 2 answers coldly; OPTION 3 says nothing and gives Cordelia room (its option text is plain words such as "Say nothing. Stay by the fire."; this reply has NO REASON row). Replies of 1 or 2 rows. Nothing is lost for good: even the cold reply leaves the door open.

TALK confrontation. Cordelia's story comes to a head. Opening: 1 NARRATOR row, then 7 to 9 SAY rows (one more NARRATOR row allowed in the middle) that tell what the journal line says in Cordelia's own words: the heart of their act-three story, plain and a little raw, never grand; Cordelia may say that something from before has found them, but must NOT name or describe the person, the act or the event behind the dark secret (no names, deeds, places or objects from the note's dark-secret section, or from its Climax and Catharsis sections): say only what it was like to stand one's ground against it; end on the turn and a question or a long silence. Three options: OPTION 1 asks Cordelia to say more; OPTION 2 is the answer most like what Cordelia needs to hear; OPTION 3 is the quiet way on, brushing it past. Three replies of 1 to 3 rows each, each ending the talk, each with a REASON row. The cool reply must still leave the Confrontation told.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line, rows in this order, nothing else:

TALK <key>
NARRATOR: <line>
SAY: <line>
SAY: <line>
OPTION 1: <what the party says>
OPTION 2: <what the party says>
OPTION 3: <what the party says>
REPLY 1
NARRATOR: <optional line>
SAY: <line>
REASON: You <what the party did>
REPLY 2
...
REPLY 3
...

TALK <key> starts a talk (the keys are given below, exactly). The rows before the first OPTION are the talk's opening. Each REPLY block holds one optional NARRATOR row first, then one or two SAY rows, then a REASON row (and an INSPIRE row where the talk asks for one). Write exactly the talks listed, in the order listed, with the row counts given.

The TALK keys, exactly: incitement, discovery, confrontation_wait, confrontation.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write. `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/cordelia_skein-voice-and-beats.md` holds the voice sheet for CORDELIA SKEIN (age, accent, pace, pet phrases, existing lines) and the character file (what Cordelia likes and dislikes, the Thread, the dark secret you must never state). `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/cordelia_skein-camp-talks.md` holds the camp talks already written for Cordelia, as voice examples: do not repeat their topics or lines.
result:
TALK incitement
NARRATOR: Cordelia sits near the embers with her lower hands spreads-out, dryin' a damp leather medical bag that smells of camphor and clove.
SAY: I slipped back into the Baggage Car before we left the rails, darling, right past that sleeping prisoner in his stripes.
SAY: Wedged beneath his iron ball was this surgical kit, holding a water-stained monograph by Doctor Hespa Marlowe titled "On the Final Stage".
SAY: She mapped all six chambers of the thoracic pump to synthesise what she called the Apex Humour.
SAY: Whoever altered my blood left the assay half-finished, and it appears I have finally found the missing pages of my own anatomy.
OPTION 1: Read the margins aloud. What was her method?
OPTION 2: Keep the notes dry. We have a long road ahead.
REPLY 1
NARRATOR: The ruby vials in her thorax catch the firelight as she traces a six-chambered diagram in crimson silk that dissolves into red mist.
SAY: Her ratios for venous distillation are remarkably crisp for a practitioner working with only two hands.
SAY: If her clinic mark leads us to her table in this valley, I intend to finish the textbook myself.
REPLY 2
NARRATOR: Cordelia folds the damp pages into oilcloth and slips them inside her coat, her four extra arms tucking neat against her ribs.
SAY: Quite right, the night air is dreadful for unbound paper and delicate calibration alike.
SAY: I shall review the doctor's thoracic diagrams in private before thehumours cool.
TALK discovery
NARRATOR: Cordelia balances a pair of scorched brass spectacles on her knee, turnin' a ciphered ledger toward the firelight with two lower fingers.
SAY: Memory's Rest was a dismal display of wasted inquiry, darling, though the crematorium ash kept Doctor Marlowe's second monograph remarkably dry.
SAY: Fascinating pathology, she documented the exact cellular stage that comes after my current state.
SAY: For years I assumed my instability was a flaw in the saline ratio, a simple failure of the blood.
NARRATOR: She taps a fingernail against the ruby glass in her chest, where the dark liquid sits thick and still.
SAY: Marlowe found that transmutative humours always decay unless the weak flesh is anchored by a mineral catalyst.
SAY: She lost her own mind to the clinic's serum before she could finish the work, forgetting her very name at the end.
SAY: Yet her final equations remain scrupulously exact, pointing to a stage where the mind can never be dragged back into the dark.
SAY: It is a complete blueprint for survival, even if I would rather not examine the price of the first draft.
OPTION 1: Does it frighten you, seeing how she ended?
OPTION 2: Her data survived. You will succeed where her method failed.
OPTION 3: Put the ledger away and get some rest.
REPLY 1
NARRATOR: Cordelia's six eyes go still as the fire pops, her voice dropping to a thin, cool whisper.
SAY: To lose one's diction and revert to a blind thing in the dark is the only pathology I cannot stomach.
SAY: That is precisely why my calibration must be cleaner than hers, down to the last drop.
REASON: You asked whether Doctor Marlowe's fate frightened me.
REPLY 2
NARRATOR: She closes the ledger with a crisp snap and adjusts the charcoal cuffs of her eight sleeves.
SAY: Spoken like a true colleague, darling, sentiment should never invalidate a sound theorem.
SAY: Marlowe lacked the proper thoracic vessels to house the reaction, whereas I am already built for the strain.
REASON: You trusted my intellect to finish Doctor Marlowe's work.
REPLY 3
NARRATOR: Cordelia slips the scorched spectacles into her pocket and smooths her waistcoat over her vials.
SAY: A sensible prescription, the soot in that place has left my throat decidedly dry.
SAY: The second stage is safely catalogued, and it will keep until we are ready to test the ratio.
REASON: You told me to put the ledger away and rest.
TALK confrontation_wait
NARRATOR: Cordelia sits a little back from the fire, her four lower arms folded tight across her waistcoat while she wipes a glass vial clean.
SAY: Before you ask about the Crooked Nightmare, darling, my notes on the final stage are sealed for the evening.
SAY: Proper bio-arcana requires discipline, brisk inquiry and a basic respect for rare specimens, qualities our company has lately neglected.
SAY: Until our methods align with reason again, I prefer to keep my observations to myself.
OPTION 1: We have been careless lately. Tell me how we fix it.
OPTION 2: Keep your notes to yourself, then.
OPTION 3: Say nothing. Stay by the fire.
REPLY 1
NARRATOR: Her lower hands unclasping a fraction, she tilts her head and studies your face in the ember glow.
SAY: Precision is a habit, darling, not an apology, so let us see how you handle the next anomaly we meet.
SAY: Once our baseline steadies, I will gladly walk you through the whole assay.
REASON: You owned your carelessness and asked how to make it right.
REPLY 2
NARRATOR: Cordelia's expression stays glass-smooth as she tucks the polishing cloth into her sleeve.
SAY: Brevity has its virtues, I suppose, when the humours are already sour.
SAY: The data will remain in my coat until you are in a mood for serious scholarship.
REASON: You told me coldly to keep my notes to myself.
REPLY 3
NARRATOR: Cordelia watches the sparks rise into the dark for a minute, keepin' her hands folded over her chest.
SAY: Silence is a clean medium, at least, and it does not cloud the glass.
SAY: We can revisit the ledger when the air between us has cleared.
TALK confrontation
NARRATOR: Cordelia unbuttons the middle cuffs of her waistcoat by the fire, watchin' the ruby vials in her thorax glint with a pale opal light.
SAY: In the Crooked Nightmare, darling, the assay finally reached its threshold, and I let the final change run through my veins.
SAY: Every equation Doctor Marlowe left promised that the last stage would burn away the unstable blood and leave a pure, untouchable vessel.
SAY: Do hold still, this will only tingle if you lean too close to the glass while the humours settle.
SAY: As the synthesis took hold, an old debt from before my surgery rose up in the dark to meet me.
NARRATOR: Her voice drops to a breathless whisper, and her four lower hands hold dead still in her lap.
SAY: I could have let the reaction erase the whole ledger, turning my mind into cold, clean stone that remembers nothing.
SAY: Instead, I held my ground against the change and forced the ratio to obey my own pulse.
SAY: The metamorphosis is complete on my terms, and my mind is permanently awake, yet the old weight in my chest has not shifted a gram.
SAY: Tell me, is a specimen truly perfected if she chooses to keep the flaw that hurts?
OPTION 1: Why keep the part that hurts when you could be free of it?
OPTION 2: Staying yourself is what made the work yours, flaw and all.
OPTION 3: You survived the change. Let that be enough for tonight.
REPLY 1
NARRATOR: Cordelia touches the lowest cuff of her sleeve with one finger, her eyes plain and level in the firelight.
SAY: Because an equation that erases its own premises is not science, darling, it is cowardice.
SAY: If I paid a ruinous tuition for this waking mind, the least I can do is stay awake to audit the bill.
REASON: You asked why I chose to keep the memory that hurts.
REPLY 2
NARRATOR: A small, crisp breath leaves her, and her four lower hands relax against the charcoal silk of her waistcoat.
SAY: That is a remarkably tidy formulation, and far kinder than any theorem I was taught.
SAY: My pulse is my own tonight, viscosity and all, and I find the calibration entirely acceptable.
REASON: You reminded me that staying myself made the work my own.
REPLY 3
NARRATOR: Cordelia fastens her waistcoat buttons from bottom to top with brisk, practiced clicks.
SAY: Practical as ever, darling, and my thoracic pressure is indeed completely stabilised.
SAY: The final stage is recorded, I am still myself, and the rest of the night is ours.
REASON: You told me that surviving the change was enough for tonight.
